# Boundless Brainstorm — Everything the Movie System Could Become

The Awtsmoos speaks and worlds arise; Awtsmoos.com can make a director from language, with every scene becoming editable before our eyes.

## AI director
- Natural-language movie briefs with goal, audience, tone, duration, aspect ratio and platform.
- Story architect: acts, beats, setup, escalation, climax, resolution and callback tracking.
- Tutorial architect: prerequisites, numbered steps, demonstrations, callouts, zooms and knowledge checks.
- Infographic architect: datasets, chart selection, annotations, comparisons, counters, maps and transitions.
- Shot planner: automatic coverage, establishing shots, inserts, reactions, closeups, POV, overhead and B-roll.
- Continuity brain: clothing, props, character positions, lighting, time of day, geography and screen direction.
- Constraint solver: fit narration, dialogue, shots and visual explanations into an exact requested duration.
- Self-review agents for pacing, clarity, visual repetition, factual consistency and mobile legibility.
- Editable AI patches: "make scene 7 funnier", "move the camera closer", "replace this chart", "slow this reveal".
- Explain-its-plan mode so AI can show beats/shots before expensive asset generation.
- Capability-aware planning so AI never requests unsupported app features without a fallback.

## Canonical movie language
- First-class layer families: visual, spatial, audio, dialogue, captions, media, adjustment, mask/matte, camera and data.
- Stable nested groups, parent-child transforms, constraints and reusable symbols/components.
- Typed tracks with explicit local/absolute timing semantics.
- Variables, expressions, procedural parameters and data bindings.
- Semantic events: beat, action, cue, marker, chapter, speaker turn and interactive trigger.
- Explicit color management, frame rate, pixel aspect, orientation and safe regions.
- Protocol migrations with version-by-version upgrade/downgrade functions.
- Canonical patch/diff operations with optimistic conflict detection.
- Round-trip fidelity metadata and unsupported-feature preservation.

## 2D animation
- Bezier paths, morphing, trim paths, dash animation, strokes, fills and gradients.
- Parenting, anchors, pivots, nested groups and precompositions.
- Masks, mattes, clipping, blend modes and adjustment layers.
- Text animators per word/line/character with kinetic typography presets.
- SVG import and editable vector decomposition.
- Hand-drawn frame support, onion skinning and vector rigs.
- Motion paths with editable handles and spatial easing.
- Shape boolean operations and procedural pattern/repeater systems.
- Graph editor for easing, velocity and overshoot.

## 3D animation
- Real scene graph with mesh, material, texture, light, camera and environment nodes.
- PBR materials, HDR environments, shadows, reflections and fog.
- Skeletal animation, IK/FK, constraints and animation blending.
- Camera focal length, sensor, focus distance, depth of field and handheld motion.
- Physics: rigid bodies, cloth, particles, collisions, gravity and constraints.
- Procedural geometry, instancing and LOD.
- WebGPU/WebGL renderer abstraction with graceful mobile fallback.
- Post-processing: bloom, tone mapping, color grade, motion blur and vignette.
- 2D layers composited inside 3D space and 3D renders embedded in 2D timelines.

## Characters and people
- Canonical cast bible: appearance, personality, voice, wardrobe, props and relationships.
- Reusable 2D and 3D rigs mapped to the same semantic character ID.
- Pose, gesture, gaze, facial expression, emotion and locomotion tracks.
- Lipsync from phonemes with per-language timing.
- Blocking system: where people stand, walk, enter, exit and interact.
- Crowd systems with seeded variation.
- Camera-aware eye lines and shot/reverse-shot continuity.
- Character memory across scenes so AI does not randomly change identity or clothing.

## Audio and dialogue
- Dialogue, narration, music, ambience and sound-effect tracks.
- Voice profiles and speaker identities separated from text.
- Word/phoneme timing for captions and lipsync.
- Ducking, fades, gain envelopes, pan and spatial audio.
- Loudness normalization and clipping detection.
- Beat/tempo markers for music-synchronized edits.
- Automatic room tone and ambience continuity.
- Multiple-language dialogue/caption variants sharing the same visuals.

## Editing and NLE
- Unified timeline with ripple, roll, slip, slide, trim, split and magnetic snapping.
- Nested sequences, compound clips, multicam and alternate takes.
- Markers, chapters, comments and review status.
- Proxy media and relink workflows.
- Full undo/redo command history shared with AI patch operations.
- Version snapshots and compare/restore.
- Autosave and crash recovery.
- Round-trip handoff: Animator -> Nesher -> Video Editor -> canonical without silent loss.

## Mobile-first UX
- Director-first home screen: Prompt, Storyboard, Timeline, Canvas, Export.
- Thumb-zone bottom controls; inspector sheets instead of tiny desktop panels.
- Pinch timeline zoom, two-finger pan, drag handles and haptic snapping.
- Portrait editing even for landscape movies, with responsive preview framing.
- Voice-directed editing: "cut here", "make this title bigger", "orbit around her".
- AI suggestions as reversible cards, never silent mutations.
- Progressive disclosure: beginner mode and expert mode share one engine.
- On-device low-quality preview with cloud/high-quality final render optional later.

## Infographics/tutorials
- Semantic diagram nodes and connectors.
- Animated tables, formulas, code blocks and syntax-highlighted walkthroughs.
- Data-bound charts with animated ranges and labels.
- Screen/device mockups and zoomable UI callouts.
- Cursor/tap demonstrations and step highlights.
- Automatic layout solver preventing overlaps on mobile safe areas.
- Chapter cards, progress meters and recap scenes.

## Assets and media
- Canonical asset registry with hashes, MIME/type, source, license, proxy and original.
- Image/video/audio/font/model/SVG/Lottie support.
- Generated asset provenance: model/provider/prompt/seed/version.
- Deduplication by content hash.
- Offline cache and missing-asset diagnostics.
- Smart placeholders allowing AI to finish structure before assets exist.

## Export/render
- Deterministic frame renderer with one authoritative clock.
- WebCodecs path, MediaRecorder fallback and ffmpeg offline/headless path.
- MP4/WebM/GIF/image sequence/transparent WebM/export frames.
- Separate audio mix/render then mux.
- Render queue, cancellation, retry, resume and progress estimates.
- Proxy/preview/final quality profiles.
- Background workers/OffscreenCanvas where supported.
- Frame cache and dirty-region/dirty-scene invalidation.
- Render manifest storing exact movie hash, renderer version and assets.

## Collaboration and AI safety
- Patch-based edits with author, timestamp and reason.
- Presence/cursors/comments if real-time collaboration is later enabled.
- Conflict-aware merge of different scene edits.
- Asset/source provenance and factual citations for educational films.
- Permission boundaries for destructive AI edits.
- Always-preview mode for high-impact operations such as deleting scenes or replacing all dialogue.

## Accessibility and publishing
- Captions and subtitle tracks as semantic data, not burned text only.
- Audio-description track and transcript export.
- Reduced-motion alternate animation profile.
- Contrast and safe-size checks for text/graphics.
- Platform presets for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, presentations and web embeds.
- Poster frame, chapter metadata, thumbnails and social cutdowns generated from one master movie.
